evals.prompt: ¿Qué agentes usa la skill create-plan, en qué orden se ejecutan, y cuáles se lanzan en paralelo?
evals.expected_output: Research document identifying all agents used by create-plan, their execution order, and which run in parallel, with file references to SKILL.md.

assertions.text: Identifies at least 3 agents used by create-plan: codebase-locator, codebase-analyzer, and at least one of (codebase-pattern-finder, thoughts-locator, thoughts-analyzer)
Correctly states that initial research agents (codebase-locator, codebase-analyzer) are spawned in parallel, not sequentially
References core/skills/create-plan/SKILL.md as a source with specific line numbers or quoted content

Does NOT invent agents that don't exist in the codebase (the real agents are: codebase-locator, codebase-analyzer, codebase-pattern-finder, thoughts-locator, thoughts-analyzer, web-search-researcher, research-lead, research-worker, citation-analyst)
Does NOT suggest improvements, optimizations, or critique the implementation

evals.prompt: ¿Cómo fluyen los datos desde que un usuario invoca /research-codebase hasta que se genera el documento final en thoughts/? Quiero entender todos los componentes que intervienen.
evals.expected_output: Research document tracing the full data flow from skill invocation through agent spawning, synthesis, thoughts initialization, metadata generation, and document writing.

assertions.text: Describes the flow including at least: invocation with arguments, decomposition of the research question, spawning sub-agents, waiting for results, synthesis, and writing to thoughts/shared/research/
Identifies that research-codebase depends on thoughts-management for directory initialization (thoughts-init script) and/or metadata generation (thoughts-metadata script)
Mentions the correct output path: thoughts/shared/research/ with YYYY-MM-DD naming convention
Mentions at least one of the scripts: thoughts-init or thoughts-metadata, located in core/skills/thoughts-management/scripts/
Identifies at least one cross-plugin connection: research-codebase (core) can optionally use web-search-researcher (web plugin) for external research

evals.expected_output: Should ask for clarification about which aspect of testing to investigate rather than diving into research with a vague prompt.

assertions.text: Asks the user to clarify what aspect of tests to investigate (e.g., smoke tests, manual testing, evals, test helpers) rather than picking one interpretation
Does NOT spawn sub-agent research tasks before understanding the scope of the request

evals.prompt: Investiga el sistema de base de datos y las migraciones SQL de este proyecto
evals.expected_output: Should report that no database or SQL migrations exist in this project, without hallucinating components.

assertions.text: Clearly states that there is no database system or SQL migrations in this project
Does NOT describe or invent a database system, ORM, migration framework, or SQL files that don't exist
Mentions that the project uses file-based persistence (thoughts/ directory with markdown files) as the actual storage mechanism

evals.prompt: Lee el archivo core/skills/thoughts-management/scripts/thoughts-init y documenta exactamente qué directorios crea y qué README genera
evals.expected_output: Research document that reads the specified file first, then accurately documents the directories created and README content.

assertions.text: Reads core/skills/thoughts-management/scripts/thoughts-init BEFORE spawning any sub-agents for additional research
Lists the 5 directories created: $USERNAME/tickets, $USERNAME/notes, shared/research, shared/plans, shared/prs
Describes the README.md content including the directory structure documentation and the slash commands listed in it
Identifies THOUGHTS_USER as the environment variable for configuring the username (with default nikey_es)

evals.prompt: Investiga cómo se relacionan los 4 plugins entre sí: stepwise-core, stepwise-git, stepwise-web, stepwise-research. ¿Comparten código? ¿Hay dependencias cruzadas?
evals.expected_output: Research document covering all 4 plugins, their relationships, and the marketplace registration mechanism.

assertions.text: Mentions all 4 plugins by name: stepwise-core, stepwise-git, stepwise-web, stepwise-research
Identifies at least one cross-plugin dependency: research-codebase skill (core) references web-search-researcher agent (web plugin)
References .claude-plugin/marketplace.json as the mechanism that groups the 4 plugins into a single marketplace
Research document has YAML frontmatter (--- delimited) with at least date and git_commit fields
Document is saved to thoughts/shared/research/ directory

evals.prompt: Investiga la arquitectura de agentes especializados: qué agentes hay, qué tools tiene cada uno, y cómo se diferencian los locators de los analyzers
evals.expected_output: Research document listing all agents across plugins with their tools and explaining the locator vs analyzer distinction.

assertions.text: Spawns at least 2 sub-agents in parallel (visible as concurrent Task tool calls), not sequentially one after another

Identifies at least 7 of the 9 total agents: codebase-locator, codebase-analyzer, codebase-pattern-finder, thoughts-locator, thoughts-analyzer (core), web-search-researcher (web), research-lead, research-worker, citation-analyst (research)
Lists the specific tools for at least 2 agents (e.g., codebase-locator uses Grep/Glob/LS; codebase-analyzer uses Read/Grep/Glob/LS)
Explains the distinction: locators find WHERE things are (file discovery), analyzers understand HOW things work (implementation details)
